messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The Weblogs (WB) genre shows a significant improvement in F1 score on the failure set after applying GBI for both syntactic parsing and SRL." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 5): quote "Weblogs (WB) 17.6 95.3 62.0 63.2 (+1.2) 20.32 44.13 47.6 57.39 (+9.39)"
2. "The Broadcast Conversation (BC) genre shows a significant improvement in F1 score on the failure set after applying GBI for both syntactic parsing and SRL." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 5): quote "Broadcast Conversation (BC) 19.3 98.8 56.4 59.0 (+2.6) 26.86 53.88 39.72 52.4 (+12.68)"
3. "The Broadcast News (BN) genre shows a significant improvement in F1 score on the failure set after applying GBI for both syntactic parsing and SRL." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 5): quote "Broadcast News (BN) 11.7 98.1 63.2 68.8 (+5.6) 18.51 55.19 39.28 50.58 (+11.3)"
4. "The Pivot Corpus (PT) genre shows the largest absolute improvement in F1 score on the failure set after applying GBI for both syntactic parsing and SRL." -- cites: E1 (Section Table 5): quote "Pivot Corpus (PT) 9.8 97.8 71.4 75.8 (+4.4) 10.01 62.34 47.19 63.69 (+16.5)"

Cited evidence:
[E1] (text, Section Table 5, page 7): Table 5: Evaluation of syntactic parser and SRL system on out-of-domain data. F1 scores are reported on the failure set . SRL model was trained on NW and the syntactic parser was trained on WSJ Section on OntoNote v5.0. Except PT, which is new and old Testament, all failure rate on out-domain data is higher than that of in-domain (11.9% for parsing and 18.1% for SRL) as suspected. The table shows that GBI can be successfully applied to resolve performance degradation on out-of-domain data.
